::: {.notes}
Allow about two minutes for Sky coverage and A joint search. Use the site map
only briefly; do not enumerate every project twice.
The map separates operating arrays from next-generation projects. P-ONE's
position denotes the Cascadia region; the final array is not equated with the
existing ONC node coordinate. TRIDENT's marker is its published design site.
These symbols do not encode instrumented volumes or funding milestones.
HUNT/B-HUNT site options and NEON are discussed on the later project slides.
HUNT and B-HUNT are not two independent capacities to sum.

For latitude phi, source declination delta and hour angle H,

$$
\cos\theta_z=\sin\phi\sin\delta+\cos\phi\cos\delta\cos H.
$$

The graph integrates the fraction of a sidereal rotation with cos(theta_z)<0,
using a surface horizon. It contains no Earth absorption, effective areas,
energy weighting, veto/reconstruction cuts or detector-depth horizon shift.
For the Galactic Centre, declination −28.94 degrees, the below-horizon time
fractions are 0% at IceCube, 63.3% at ARCA and 74.8% at Baikal-GVD.
IceCube's southern sky is not inaccessible: contained-event and starting-track
selections also provide coverage. Long below-horizon paths can suppress
very-high-energy neutrinos; geometrical visibility is not detection efficiency.

The last tab is the published ANTARES–IceCube joint southern-sky analysis.
For E^-2 the five-sigma discovery flux of the joint analysis is lower than
that of the better single sample by up to a factor of about 1.7 (digitized
curves); the paper quotes improvements of up to about two in sensitivity,
depending on the spectrum. This
analysis found no significant source. The curves are not current KM3NeT or
GVD sensitivities and not proposed-detector forecasts. The graph is a
lecture-style redraw of the digitized published curves, with the same quantity,
axes and samples (`assets/joint-search/README.md`).

[Joint ANTARES–IceCube search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04412);
[GVD site](https://indico.cern.ch/event/378423/contributions/900413/attachments/1155595/1660951/3_zhan_Baikal_VLVnT_status.pdf);
[P-ONE infrastructure](https://www.oceannetworks.ca/news-and-stories/stories/onc-coengineers-key-infrastructure-for-pacific-deep-sea-neutrino-telescope/);
[TRIDENT design](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41550-023-02087-6);
[Network studies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07549).
:::
